item.title: Governance in Family Firms: In Search of New Paradigms?
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites research on how governance systems in family firms are evolving in response to contemporary challenges including increased government intervention, technological disruption from AI, and global geopolitical instability. The issue seeks to deepen understanding of the mechanisms through which family firms navigate these complex environments while maintaining their distinctive characteristics.

Contributions should explore how various governance structures—such as boards, ownership arrangements, leadership models, succession planning, and family-specific governance processes—enable family firms to generate value, ensure operational continuity, and successfully adapt to rapidly changing business conditions.

Appel publié par Corporate Governance An International Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Reform to Renewal: Succession, Socioemotional Wealth, and the Future of Chinese Family Businesses
item.content:encoded:
James Vardaman, University of Memphis

Feigu Zhou, University of Montevallo

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

Shuai Jin, Jiangsu University

Weiwen Li, Sun Yat-sen University

This special collection examines Chinese family businesses navigating intergenerational succession as they approach the 50-year anniversary of China's economic reforms. The collection addresses how family firms balance continuity with renewal as founders transfer leadership to successors, focusing particularly on socioemotional wealth—the noneconomic priorities that family firms pursue, such as preserving family control, maintaining family identity, and ensuring transgenerational continuity.

Chinese family firms provide a distinctive context for advancing family business theory. Unlike Western family enterprises that evolved within stable institutional environments, contemporary Chinese firms emerged after market reforms and now experience large-scale waves of succession amid shifts in economic institutions, governance expectations, and societal values. Successors assume leadership while navigating the coexistence of traditional Confucian principles emphasizing family continuity with modern market logics, professional management practices, and global stakeholder expectations.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Founder succession and leadership transfer in post-reform family firms
  • Successor identity formation and legitimacy
  • Preservation versus erosion of SEW during succession
  • Tensions between family control and professionalization
  • Emotional attachment, family identity, and transgenerational intentions
  • SEW and strategic renewal
  • Long-term consequences of Reform and Opening for family enterprise
  • State–family business relationships over time
  • Family and nonfamily employee experiences
  • Shared identity and organizational identification

item.title: International Marketing in Family Business: Identity, Strategy and Growth
item.content:encoded:
Family businesses are a dominant organisational form worldwide and play a critical role in shaping employment, investment and long-term regional development. They are also key participants in cross-border activity. Recent studies show that internationalisation by family-controlled businesses is pervasive enough to affect aggregate patterns of global competition, rather than being a marginal exception. Existing research has paid great attention to examining whether and to what extent family involvement alters the degree, speed, and performance of internationalisation. In contrast, the marketing dimension of family businesses' international activity, in terms of how the family imprint travels to foreign customers and channels, remains comparatively underdeveloped in the literature.

Appel publié par International Marketing Review. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
